There we go. Goodbye, CATS. As we're on Side B now, I'll break kayfabe with you: last time, CATS wasn't running in the background. That's not how SPNATI works. I was just cycling him through random facial expressions, and don't want to go through the same effort again. This is the B-Side, we have fun here, we chill here. Without further ado, let's get into the live Q&A.
Question One: How did you feel while learning the tools to make this project?

Like shit, to be honest. Credit where it's due, the character editor is about as smooth and painless as something like this could reasonably be, but it still ain't easy. And don't even get me started on Kisekae. Every time I open that program I get acid reflux. I have no idea how the artists out there manage it.
Question Two: Did you use any guides? Get any guidance from any user in particular?

That's a great question, and I'm glad you asked it. I don't feel comfortable giving my opinion on who's the best without going down the list first, so let's just run through our options before we narrow it down to a winner. First of all, there's Twilight Sparkle. Classic pony. Everyone knows Twilight, everyone knows what she's about, but just for the people in the back I'll recap her deal real quick. Twilight Sparkle is the protagonist and lead character of My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic, the animated series for the fifth (and by far most popular) generation of MLP. She's a studious bookworm who has extreme amounts of booksmarts, but lacks in the social skills to back it up. Her element in the Elements of Harmony is Magic, which I personally think is a bit of a cop-out, but what do I know, eh? Over the series she gradually grows as a person and forms plentiful friendships, coming out of her shell and forming the glue that sticks the rest of the inhabitants of Ponyville together in terms of matters of friendship. However, she's not my favourite. I like girls with glasses and all, and I respect her studiousity, but she's just too... basic? Y'know? What's Twilight Sparkle got going for her? Like actually. Please, tell me. What does Twilight Sparkle have going for her?
Question Four: Would you make CATS for real if someone asked for it?

Great, and absolutely. She's a great artist, very talented, always willing to put up with whatever new bullshit idea I had. Very painless experience, great time, and a great person from the personal discussions we've had. I'll never not trust an A.B.A. fan.
Question Three: How was the experience working with Bluejae? Is she cool?

I'll be honest with you: I cannot remember. I'm sorry. I know I pored over the character writing guide a fair bit, and I was frequently asking for technical support in the devcord, but that's about it. Again, apologies.

Well, there already was a remaster that changed the lore, but I digress. To be honest, if I met a second person on all of planet the earth who gave a shit about Zero Wing I think I'd be too busy making out with them and giving them all of my money to get into lore discussions.

Which is funny, because I hadn't even been born when most of them came out. When I was a kid, Vine was the new hotness. What the hell a Vine kiddie was doing browsing old KnowYourMeme articles all day, I'll never know.

Something to do with the autism, presumably. Anyway, yes, I was very much into retro memes. Advice animals, Bad Luck Brian, Peanut Butter Jelly Time (or as we call it in the UK, Peanut Butter Jam Time), you name it and I've laughed at it.

But I've always had a particular soft spot for All Your Base. I'm a huge fan of cheesy sci-fi (for my sins), and Zero Wing (even without the dodgy translation) is some of the cheesiest sci-fi around. Plus, CATS objectively looks pretty cool.
I'll spare you the details of how I ended up in SPNATI town, but the way things ended up I wanted to contribute really bad but only had time for an April Fools. And so, CATS was born!

First problem quickly emerges: Who the *hell* is CATS? No, like, seriously, who is this dude? If you've never played Zero Wing before (great game by the way, fiver on steam, seriously consider picking it up) you might think this is a simple question to answer. But it's not!

You see, CATS and Zero Wing are from a different era in gaming. One before lore, before franchises, before any of that nonsense. Nobody cared about source accuracy! Nobody cared about consistency among material! Nobody was gonna *read* that shit anyway!

So, it comes as little surprise the era of gaming that told us Megaman lived in the city of Monsteropolis couldn't get the story straight about CATS. Is he an alien? A cyborg? An AI? A space pirate? An alien AI space pirate cyborg? Is his name even CATS, or is CATS the name of the organisation he represents? Who knows!
There, see? Not exactly the perfect sexyman body.
Second problem quickly emerges: This guy doesn't have a cock. No penis. Not a willy to be seen. He's all cape, some face, nothing else. Actually, let me see if I can't...

In the end, I decided to just use 'em all! Everything's canon! Who cares! In my personal world, CATS is an alien from the far reaches of space who merged with a rogue AI and now runs a space pirate organisation also called CATS.

First of all, he's a smug son of a bitch. I bet he's probably doing the smug pose right now as you read this. Something like 60% of all his lines use that one pose, I think? I know it was a lot closer to 90% before I went back and forced myself to show off more of Bluejae's great posing.
In short, he's a bit of a prick.

What's next... let me see... Ah, of course, the writing. It's a lot harder than you'd think, you know? There's a very specific diction you have to tap into, a deeply unique register. You can't just put random engrish in, it needs to be stuff CATS would say, if that makes sense. He's not just a bunch of funny words, he is actually a character.

Where was I? Oh, yes, we'd just addressed the modelling. I did genuinely debate giving this guy a Fucked Up Alien Cock for a short while, but in the end realised it just wasn't worth it. He's an April Fools, you can get silly with it out here. More on that later.

But yeah, he's smug. He's deeply self-centred, he's cocky, a bit vain, he carries himself like he's royalty, he doesn't seem to even think it possible that he could lose, and his cool shatters very quickly when he does lose.

But this is what a lot of people miss about him. As I mentioned before, he's not just "broken english", he has a voice. A very garbled voice, yes, but a voice nonetheless. And one that's incredibly difficult to write for.

I started out trying to write in his voice, but quickly realised how infeasible that'd be. By the end of things, I'd established a process: I'd write a line in plain english, then... CATS-ify it, for lack of a better term.
Here, let's give an example. "Joshua turned on the microwave". Normal sentence, plain and simple. Listeners at home, try and CATS-ify this sentence, and we'll reconvene shortly to compare answers.

Now that you've done yours, I'll walk you through me doing mine. First of all, we want to shuffle the words around. Re-order the sentence, make it follow different grammar rules. There's no hard and fast here, just go on how it feels to read. In this case, it leaves us with "The microwave is turned on by Joshua".
Next, let's drop some words and suffixes. "Microwave is turn on by Josh".
Now, add some techno-babble and single quotation marks, re-order it again as needed, and put it all in caps. "'MICROWAVE SYSTEM' IS ACTIVATE BY 'JOSH' FORCES". See, now you're starting to understand!

The stripping phases are one of my favourite parts of CATS. As mentioned before, I'd had some trouble deciding what to do for stripping, when I realised something: SPNATI characters have 8 stages and masturbation. Zero Wing has 8 stages and a final boss gauntlet. What if I could find a way to link the two?

Final topic: the stripping phases. Originally I'd planned to play this while he stripped, but ran into some Technical Bumps, so it's just been strapped onto the end of the commentary. My apologies for the bumpy pacing of this.

Now, I won't act like it it isn't very fun to write for CATS, but it is also undeniably a pain in the arse at times. When the character's whole gimmick is comprehensibility, how do you make it comprehensible? As you've just seen, it's quite the hassle.

Where to begin... well, at the start, I suppose. All Your Base is a really important video to me. It, along with other classics like This is Sparta! Last techno remix and Why is the Rum Gone? - Remix provided the soundtrack for much of my youth.

Anyway, I think that's all I have to say on CATS. Thanks for listening, and I'll let you get back to your game now. To access side B of this commentary track, set your name to "Aleiste". There won't be as much on that track, just a Q&A with a member of the public. From the bottom of my heart, thank you for playing CATS, and remember:
